request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**How it works:**
- **New audit method:** I added `Audit.recordOnCommit` in `Audit.java`. It holds the line until the database change has been saved for good, then appends it. So a change that gets refused, or that fails partway, writes no line. That covers today's checks (a duplicate name, an amount like `1.005`) and any rules added later. It also means lines go into the file in the order the changes are saved.
- **People:** `PersonService.add` and `edit` write `PERSON_ADDED` and `PERSON_EDITED` lines with the saved name and grade. `edit` now takes the signed-in user as an argument, passed in by `PersonController`.
- **Claims:** `ClaimService.add` and `edit` now take the user too, and write `CLAIM_ADDED` and `CLAIM_EDITED` lines. Each line has the person's name, the amount with two decimals and the date as yyyy-mm-dd. When no date is entered, the line shows the date the claim was saved with (the sheet's today).

An edit writes a line even when nothing actually changes, such as setting a grade to the value it already has. The tests expect this.

The front end didn't need any changes.
